chosen.premise: Kabuto molts every three days, and each new shell becomes harder than the last.
chosen.hook: Kabuto gets a harder shell every three days.
chosen.visualIdea: Rapidly cycle through shed shells labeled day 3, day 6, and day 9 as armor thickens.
chosen.note: A highly concrete, unusual biological rule with a strong visual progression. The cited Sword entry directly supports both the three-day interval and increasingly harder shells.

candidates.premise: Kabuto is called almost entirely extinct, yet its sightings are fairly common in some places.
candidates.hook: Kabuto is almost extinct—but sightings can be fairly common.
candidates.visualIdea: Split the screen between an 'almost extinct' stamp and a map area filling with Kabuto sighting markers.
candidates.note: A compelling contradiction directly supported by the Pokédex: nearly extinct overall, yet fairly common in some places. It may need careful wording so “common” is not overstated beyond the source.

candidates.premise: While hiding on the seafloor, Kabuto watches with eyes on its back—and those eyes can glow.
candidates.hook: Kabuto hides on the seafloor, but its eyes are on its back.
candidates.visualIdea: Reveal Kabuto from underneath a seafloor hiding spot, then illuminate the eyes on its back.
candidates.note: The back-eye reveal is distinctive and easy to stage visually. It combines several supported details, though the hook is somewhat familiar and less surprising than the molt.

candidates.premise: Kabuto has not changed at all for 300 million years, making evolution look like a failed experiment.
candidates.hook: What if a Pokémon survived 300 million years without changing?
candidates.visualIdea: Show a fossil-to-Kabuto timeline spanning 300 million years, with Kabuto's silhouette unchanged.
candidates.note: The 300-million-year claim is strongly supported, but “making evolution look like a failed experiment” is an unsupported interpretation, and the premise is less concrete than the molt mechanic.

candidates.premise: Kabuto is resurrected from fossils found on what was once the ocean floor.
candidates.hook: Kabuto's fossil was found where the ocean floor used to be.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate an ancient ocean floor becoming rock, then crack open the fossil to reveal revived Kabuto.
candidates.note: The fossil and ancient ocean-floor transformation are well supported and visually clear, but fossil resurrection is a common Pokémon premise and not especially unique to Kabuto.

candidates.premise: At level 40, Kabuto evolves into Kabutops while keeping the same Rock/Water typing.
candidates.hook: At level 40, Kabuto evolves—but its two types stay exactly the same.
candidates.visualIdea: Level counter climbs to 40 as Kabuto transforms into Kabutops, with Rock and Water badges remaining.
candidates.note: The level and unchanged typing are precise and fully supported, but evolution at level 40 and retained typing are ordinary mechanics rather than a strong Kabuto-specific story.

rounds.request: The chosen angle is strong enough. A stronger alternative would need an equally specific Kabuto-only rule or contradiction, with direct Pokédex support and a visually escalating payoff.
